newsitem.title: UK: UK speed record hopeful sets off again for Jordan.
newsitem.headline: UK speed record hopeful sets off again for Jordan.

text.p: Land speed record-holder Richard Noble sets off for the Jordanian desert on Tuesday to complete high speed trials with his supersonic Thrust SSC car.

The British team is preparing for an assault on the sound barrier in September in direct competition with former record holder Craig Breedlove and his Spirit of America car in Nevada's Black Rock desert.
Noble, who holds the land speed record of 633.47 mph (1,019.44 kph), said the Thrust trials in Jordan would be aimed at running the 9.5-tonne, 110,000-horsepower car up to 600 mph.
"On completion of the trials, the team will return to the UK to prepare for the supersonic head-to-head race against the Spirit of America team," Noble said in a statement.

Unforeseen heavy rains brought Noble's efforts to test the car on Jordan's Al Jafr desert to an abrupt halt last November, thwarting preparations to take the jet-powered Thrust through the 750 mph sound barrier.
Thrust, powered by two engines from a Phantom warplane, is designed to exceeed 850 mph, but so far it has not exceeded a relatively sedate 300 mph.
The Al Jafr desert's previous claim to fame was as the location where Omar Sharif was filmed emerging from the haze in a celebrated scene in the classic film Lawrence of Arabia.
Noble's other rival, Australian former drag racer Roscoe McGlashan, is moving his Aussie Invader 3 team to Lake Gardiner in South Australia for land speed record runs.
